BBC News — published 2026-09-26T05:07:48Z = 06:07 BST, Sat 26 Sep 2026. By Kate Whannel, political reporter.

HEADLINE: Burnham not doing enough to boost growth, says Starmer ally

A cabinet minister under Sir Keir Starmer has said Andy Burnham's government is not focused enough on boosting economic growth and needs to act with "more urgency".

Speaking to the BBC two months after being sacked in Burnham's cabinet reshuffle upon entering office, Peter Kyle said he wasn't making a "criticism" but "pointing to the potential that we have as a country and as a government".

QUOTE (Peter Kyle, former business secretary, MP for Hove and Portslade, to BBC's Laura Kuenssberg):
"If the destination means prosperity, it means freedom for people to do new things, and it means security for people and families, then why wouldn't we put our foot down and get there quicker."

QUOTE (Peter Kyle):
"We might need to look and have honest conversations with unions about how we sequence some of the rights going forward in order to make sure that we get growth into the economy in the shorter term."

QUOTE (Peter Kyle, asked if there was enough focus on growth in the government):
"I don't think there is and that isn't a criticism - it is pointing to the potential that we have as a country and as a government. I think we need to up our ambition, I think that we need to act with more urgency when it comes to economic growth."

FACTS:
- Comes as Labour prepares to gather in Liverpool for its annual conference.
- Burnham will address the conference on Tuesday and has said his speech would leave nobody in any doubt about "what I'm trying to do in this role."
- Kyle served as science secretary and later business secretary under Starmer; now a backbencher, MP for Hove and Portslade.
- Kyle suggested government should accept "short-term" pain for growth, including a possible delay to expanding workers' rights. The Employment Rights Act was passed in December 2025 but some changes are not due to come into force until next year.
- Kyle also suggested a "tax growth test" measuring the impact of each tax on the economy, and asking government experts to review "obstacles" to growth.
- Chancellor John Healey is due to give his first Budget on 28 October but faces rising debt costs and warnings of slower growth.
- OECD expects the UK economy to grow by 1%, slightly less than the 1.1% previously forecast.
- Earlier this week Starmer ally Darren Jones told the New Statesman he thought Starmer should have been given more time in office, criticising "this modern approach of getting queasy and then just changing [leader] too rapidly". Jones, former chief secretary to the prime minister, added: "Irrespective of what's happened and how, we want it to be successful, and we have a collective responsibility to help make that the case." And: "We, as backbenchers in the PLP, are looking to... Andy and his team to get that right. We want them to get it right."
